flow.title: How a document becomes a digital form
flow.validate: Checks the filename, size, format and contents.
flow.extract: Reads text and spreadsheet cells or detects fields on a page image.
flow.compile: Groups fields into sections, applies rules and returns the form configuration as JSON.
flow.web: Accepts the upload, requests conversion and displays the form alongside the document.
flow.database: Stores metadata and links each document to its result.
flow.storage: Stores the source file and resulting JSON in S3-compatible storage.

about.eyebrow: COI challenge · Working proof of concept
about.title: FORMIQ — digitising public service forms
about.description: FORMIQ helps public officials build an online service from a form published in a public information bulletin. It reads the fields and generates a JSON configuration that an official can review before import.
about.scopeTitle: From source document to electronic form

import.title: Upload a document
import.description: The REST API accepts one PDF, DOC, DOCX, ODS, XLSX, JPG, JPEG or PNG file per request. It checks the filename, size and whether the contents match the extension. In the web interface, officials can upload up to eight files at once and track their progress in the queue.

structure.title: Fields, dictionaries and conditions
structure.description: The generator groups fields into sections and pages by topic and links recognised fields to dictionaries and initial values. On the tax overpayment form, selecting a bank transfer reveals the account number field.

review.title: Review and correct
review.description: Officials can compare the source document with the JSON or open an editable form containing the extracted values. An invalid PESEL number is highlighted in place. Officials can save corrections and download the JSON.

runtime.title: Deployment and storage
runtime.description: Pyworker processes the file for the duration of the request. The web interface stores the original and its result for later review. Docker supports running models locally. In development mode, Qwen processes images through Eden AI.
